blocks.x: M. Night Shyamalan Officially Confirms the Fate of His Superhero Franchise [Exclusive]

blocks.x: Image via Touchstone Pictures

While M. Night Shyamalan has been a polarizing director throughout his time in Hollywood, it can't be denied that he's always had unique ideas. The two-time Oscar nominee broke out in a big way in 1999 with the release of his psychological thriller The Sixth Sense, featuring one of film's all-time great twists that flips its most iconic line on its head. Just one year later, he'd return with Unbreakable, his take on a superhero film in a time before the MCU, The Dark Knight, and the revitalization of comic book movies. Reuniting with Bruce Willis and featuring Samuel L. Jackson, he delivered what was, at the time, a more nuanced look than most at the nature of superpowers and what it means to have them in a complicated world centered on a man learning the bounds of his abilities. Split and Glass helped expand the world and themes into a complete trilogy with a climactic showdown between the Overseer, the Horde (James McAvoy), and Elijah Price.

Yet, there have been questions about the potential for more stories within the wider Unbreakable universe. The demand for mature superhero media has grown over the years, with The Boys and Invincible earning high marks for how they confront the harsh realities of superpowered beings, and the video game Dispatch taking a more grounded approach to the relationships between villains reforming as heroes in a society they're naturally a part of. Shyamalan has previously kept the door open for the right story, but he's kept busy with other projects since, from Old to Trap and Knock at the Cabin. Now, for several reasons, he's unlikely to release another film in his comic-inspired series.

During a conversation with Collider's Steve Weintraub to discuss his sweeping retrospective at this year's Beyond Fest at American Cinematheque, he was asked if there was a chance of another entry in the universe, even if it involved new characters. He responded simply, "I don't think so."

He did admit that he had some ideas for similarly superpowered characters that could theoretically go through similar thematic journeys to that of Willis' Overseer as they wrestled with their abilities, but he's not necessarily thinking about them in the context of Unbreakable. It's also not a world he believes he can revisit without the retired Willis involved.

"Partly because Bruce [Willis] is so central to that. But I have characters in my head that pop into my head, and one in particular that could easily coexist in that universe. It just pops into my head, 'Oh, wow. That's a really cool character that has a power.' And so this one that I have in my head that popped in could easily be in that world, but I don't want to jam it in and force it into something. It's more I just like thinking of contemporary supernatural characters that could easily be in a comic book."

One is still working out who it is while the fighting happens. And one has no powers at all, plus no intention of playing fair. Eight questions decide where you actually belong.

Your Team Is…

Four teams, four completely different reasons to put yourself in danger
for strangers. This is the roster you actually belong on, what they would want from you, and what it
would cost you to stay.
Marvel Studios · The Avengers · Since 2012
The Avengers

You belong where the stakes are largest and the personalities are
loudest. This is a team of people who are all used to being the most important person in the
room, which is exactly why it works and exactly why it keeps nearly falling apart.

The Avengers are not friends who became a team. They are a team that slowly and
reluctantly became friends, and you would recognise every stage of that process.

You can hold your own among big egos without needing to win every exchange, which is the
real entry requirement here.

The arguing is part of the method. This group does its best thinking mid-disagreement,
usually at volume, usually in a very expensive building.
When the sky opens, they are who shows up. You would want to be standing in that line.
Marvel · X-Men · Since 1963
The X-Men

You have never had the luxury of being thanked for this. The
X-Men protect a world that has never once been comfortable with them existing, and something
in you understands exactly why they keep doing it anyway.

This is the only team on the list whose central conflict is not a villain. It is being
wanted gone by the same people they keep saving.

You know what it is to be the outsider in a room and to decide, anyway, that you will
not make yourself smaller so everyone else is comfortable.

The X-Men are the most genuine found family in comics. People arrive with nowhere else
to go and are never once asked to explain themselves.
You would not be joining for the glory. There has never been any.
DC · Teen Titans · Since 1964
The Teen Titans

You do not want colleagues, you want your people. The Titans are
the team where the friendship came first and the world-saving turned up afterwards as an
inconvenient side effect.

Every Titan is somebody's sidekick who decided to stop being one. That decision, not the
villain of the week, is what the team is actually about.

You would be joining people who are all working themselves out at the same time as you,
which is far less lonely than being the only one.

The Titans lose regularly. Then they eat together and come back better, which is a more
honest model of growing up than any other team here manages.
The tower would be loud, chaotic, and the first place that ever felt like yours.
Prime Video · The Boys · Since 2019
The Boys

You are not asking who to trust. You worked out the answer a
while ago and it was nobody in a cape. This is where you go once you have decided the people
in charge need watching, and that nobody else is going to do it.

The Boys have no powers, no mandate and no funding. What they have is leverage,
patience, and a very high tolerance for consequences.
https://static0.colliderimages.com/assets/images/sr-db-logo-icon-colored-dark.svg?v=1.9

You are the person in the room who notices the thing everybody else has quietly agreed
not to mention.

This is not a heroic team and it has never pretended otherwise. It is a group of damaged
people doing necessary work in ways nobody would call clean.
You would not sleep well. You would keep going anyway.
↻ RETAKE THE QUIZ
M. Night Shyamalan's Next Project Is a Collaboration With Nicholas Sparks

Shyamalan has been relatively quiet since Trap debuted in 2024, but his absence from the big screen won't last much longer. On February 5, 2027, he'll release his next film, Remain, a romantic supernatural thriller that emerged from an idea he developed with romance novelist extraordinaire Nicholas Sparks. The two will bring their own touches to the story in their respective mediums, making both the film and book a unique take on the same core story that plays to their respective strengths. Jake Gyllenhaal will lead the cast as Tate Gordon, an architect designing a summer home for his friend in Cape Cod, still haunted by the death of his sister. He experiences a jolt of life, however, upon meeting a curious young woman named Wren (Phoebe Dynevor). Shyamalan will also have a role to play in front of the camera, joining Julie Hagerty, Tracy Ifeachor, Jay O. Sanders, and Ashley Walters among the supporting group.
Stay tuned here at Collider for more from our conversation with Shyamalan.
